name: claude-mem
tagline: Persistent memory for your AI agent - it remembers what you worked on, what you decided, and what you like, across sessions.
sentence: Install claude-mem and your AI coding agent remembers your preferences, past decisions and project context between sessions - like giving it a notebook that carries over.

visual.alt: An animated preview of claude-mem in a terminal: the agent retrieves stored memories about the user's project preferences and coding style, then uses them in its response.
visual.caption: The agent pulling stored memories into a session - preferences and decisions carry over automatically.

board.say: Every time you start a new session with your AI coding agent, it forgets everything - your preferences, your past decisions, the context you built up. You repeat yourself constantly.
board.eg: You told Claude Code last week that you prefer Tailwind over CSS modules, but today it suggests CSS modules again because it has no memory of that conversation.

board.say: claude-mem runs automatically at the start and end of every session, loading and saving memories.
board.eg: Start a new Claude Code session and the agent automatically retrieves your stored preferences, decisions and project context - no manual recall needed.

board.say: Your conversations with the agent - it captures preferences, decisions and important context as you work.
board.eg: When you say 'I prefer functional components over class components,' claude-mem stores that as a permanent preference.

board.say: It stores memories in a local database and automatically retrieves the relevant ones at the start of each session.
steps: At the end of a session, 5 lifecycle hooks capture preferences, decisions and context and store them in a local SQLite database with Chroma for search
At the start of the next session, it retrieves the memories most relevant to what you're working on
Tools let you search, add or edit memories manually if you want to
board.eg: The README demo: the agent remembers that your project uses a specific testing framework and applies that context without being told again.

board.say: An AI agent that gets better the more you use it - because it remembers.

outputs.eg: Your coding style, framework choices and project conventions, applied automatically in every session
Past architectural decisions and their reasoning, so the agent doesn't suggest what you already rejected

before: Every new session starts from zero. The agent doesn't know your preferences, your project's conventions, or what you decided last week.
You repeat the same context at the start of every session - framework choices, coding style, project structure.
after: The agent remembers your preferences, decisions and project context across sessions - it gets better the more you use it.
No manual recall needed. Relevant memories load automatically when you start a new session.
uses_note: claude-mem is over a year old with 98.9K stars. Real named uses from outside the maker's team are hard to find in public - most adoption is through Claude Code where the tool works silently in the background.

pulse.gain: +3.2K stars this week, +5.2K in 30 days. 98.9K total. Still climbing after 13 months.
pulse.history_note: Created Aug 31, 2025. Steady growth over 13 months.

steps: [Read the claude-mem README](https://github.com/thedotmack/claude-mem) to understand how the lifecycle hooks work and what gets stored.
Install claude-mem in Claude Code and start a session. Work on something and state a preference (like 'I prefer TypeScript over JavaScript').
Start a new session and ask the agent what it remembers about your preferences. Check that it recalls what you told it.
try.paste:
/skillspector https://github.com/thedotmack/claude-mem

If that scan passes: install claude-mem, work through a short session, state a preference, then start a new session and check if the agent remembers it. 10 minutes max.

footprint.disk: No data found for exact install size. Uses SQLite and Chroma for local storage - the database grows with your memories.
footprint.memory: No data found. Runs as a plugin inside Claude Code.
footprint.runs_on: Wherever Claude Code runs (Mac, Windows, Linux).

best_for: You use Claude Code daily and are tired of repeating your preferences, project conventions and past decisions at the start of every session
You want your AI agent to get better over time by learning from your conversations
skip_if: You prefer to control exactly what context the agent sees - claude-mem captures memories automatically, which may include things you'd rather forget
You already use a manual memory system (like CLAUDE.md files) that gives you full control over what the agent knows

alternatives.name: CLAUDE.md files
alternatives.line: Claude Code's built-in memory files. You write the context by hand, so you control exactly what the agent knows - but nothing is captured automatically.

alternatives.name: Obsidian
alternatives.line: A personal knowledge base you manage yourself. Not AI-agent memory, but a structured way to keep notes your agent can read.

watch: **CMEM cryptocurrency token.** The creator endorses a CMEM token associated with the project. The open-source tool works without the token, but its existence is worth knowing.
**Paid tier after 30 days.** CMEM Pro costs $30/month after a 30-day free trial. The core open-source features work without it, but some advanced features are gated.
**By Alex Newman (thedotmack).** A solo developer project with 3,222 commits. The Apache-2.0 license means the code is open, but long-term maintenance depends on one person.
**Automatic memory capture raises privacy questions.** The tool captures preferences and decisions from your conversations and stores them locally. Review what it stores periodically.
